steps.title: Pointing Candidates
steps.body: When every note for a digit inside a 3×3 box sits on the same row or column, that box 'points' down the line. We can then clear that digit from the rest of that row/column outside the box.

steps.title: Set the Stage
steps.body: We'll solve the obvious singles and keep notes on so the pattern stands out. Pointing Candidates often appear after a few easy moves.

steps.title: Highlight the 9s
steps.body: Tap any filled 9. Highlighting a digit makes it easier to see where that number already appears in the grid, which helps spot pointing patterns.

steps.title: Find the Pointing 9
steps.body: In the middle-right box, the only 9 candidates are stacked in the same column. That forces the 9 for this box to live in that column, so 9 can't appear elsewhere along it. Tap the two 9-candidate cells to apply the move.

steps.title: What Changed
steps.body: Those two cells pointed down the column and removed 9 from the other candidates in that column. Pointing always eliminates a digit outside the box that created the pattern.

steps.title: Finish the Puzzle
steps.body: Keep using Pointing Candidates (and singles) to wrap up this puzzle. Hint: The pattern is easiest to see after selecting a filled cell!
